description: Real ROCBA run: TASK-001 escalation_required from CONTRA-001 comparing 'PowerShell EventID 4104 ... event #1' vs 'event #2' (same artifact/field, different text) -> flagged as same_artifact_field_value_mismatch. title: Re-ingest extracted/derived artifacts into the plannable input set (manifest-vs-derived seam)
description: GAP 2 (Epic H). The planner reads ONLY evidence_manifest.json (route_manifest), never derived_artifacts.json. extract_artifacts_from_image writes carved files to run/evidence/extracted/ as DerivedArtifacts (provenance: source-image sha + NTFS inode), and 'siftmesh decompress' (b2m.1) writes a decompressed memory image there too — but plan/dispatch/critique never see them. So analyzing extracted/decompressed artifacts today needs a SECOND init-case over evidence/extracted/ (custody-clean, but two run dirs). This is the same manifest-vs-derived seam deferred in G9 (derived-artifact coverage). The 'one continuous run' answer belongs to Epic H's siftmesh run state machine.
design: Add an explicit, provenance-preserving ingest-derived step (a primitive the planner/run uses): read derived_artifacts.json and add carved/decompressed files to the PLANNABLE input set as DERIVED inputs, each carrying its source-image sha + inode (or DECOMP-NNN source) — NEVER silently merged into the intake manifest (keep 'sealed at intake' vs 'we produced' distinct, so the chain claim -> tool_call -> extracted file (sha) -> source image (sha+inode) stays unbroken). Then siftmesh run sequences extract -> ingest-derived -> plan -> dispatch -> critique -> report as one governed flow. Do NOT naive-merge derived files into evidence_manifest.json (that muddies custody). Subsumes the G9 deferred derived-artifact coverage. Spine-gated: implement during Epic H, not before.
acceptance_criteria: An ingest-derived primitive makes extracted (extract_artifacts_from_image) and decompressed (siftmesh decompress) artifacts visible to plan/dispatch/critique within the SAME run, each as a derived input retaining full provenance back to its source (image sha + inode, or DECOMP source archive); evidence_manifest.json (intake seal) is NOT mutated; siftmesh run can drive image/memory cases end-to-end without a manual second init-case; G9 coverage detection accounts for derived artifacts.
notes: Discovered while answering how a user runs SIFTMesh on a real dataset (Rocba-Memory.zip + rocba-cdrive.e01). Pairs with b2m.1 (GAP 1, decompress CLI). Leave OPEN until Epic H is reached (do not claim now).

title: siftmesh decompress: first-class CLI for compressed memory captures (zip/7z → derived image)
description: GAP 1 (Epic D-H hardening). analyze_memory / the analyze-memory CLI require an ALREADY-decompressed image (resolved_source + detect_format; docstring: 'typically the run's evidence/extracted dir where the decompressed image lives'). The hard logic — memory_access.decompress() (nested zip->7z->image, zip-slip guard, magic detect, fail-closed on missing 7z) — already exists and is fully tested (tests/EPIC_D_TESTS/test_memory_access.py), but NO CLI command wires it and analyze_memory never calls it. A user with Rocba-Memory.zip therefore has no first-class path to a decompressed image. This adds a 'siftmesh decompress RUN_DIR --archive <rel> [--evidence <root>]' evidence-prep primitive (NOT an MCP tool; allowlist stays exactly 10) that decompresses into run/evidence/extracted/, registers a DerivedArtifact (provenance: source archive + sha) under a DECOMP-NNN id, records a derived_written custody event + orchestration events, and prints the next analyze-memory invocation. Reuses memory_access.decompress (no re-implementation).
design: CLI command in siftmesh_core/cli.py mirroring extract-artifacts/analyze-memory; reusable helper siftmesh_core/evidence/decompress.decompress_archive(run, *, archive, evidence_root) -> DecompressOutcome (so Epic H run can call it). Resolve archive read-only via resolved_source; dest via safe_write_path(run, evidence/extracted, evidence_root); call memory_access.decompress; mint DECOMP-NNN by scanning derived_artifacts.json (keeps TOOL-NNN/tool_calls.jsonl clean — decompress is evidence-prep, not a forensic tool); append_derived + append_event(event_type=derived_written, action=decompress) + log_event decompress_start/done. Fail closed (BackendUnavailableError) on missing 7z; no schema/allowlist/config change (derived_written event_type already exists; 7z discovered via PATH; doctor already probes 7z).
acceptance_criteria: decompress command registered + in --help; decompresses a (CI-safe plain) zip into run/evidence/extracted/; one DerivedArtifact record (source_artifact, derived_sha256, tool_call_id=DECOMP-NNN) + one derived_written custody event; decompressed image resolves via resolved_source(run, evidence/extracted/<name>) for analyze-memory; fails closed with exit 1 + a 7z message when 7z is absent and a .7z member is present; rejects an archive escaping the evidence root; allowlist stays 10; ruff/format/mypy/pytest green.
close_reason: Implemented siftmesh decompress CLI + evidence/decompress.decompress_archive helper; reuses tested memory_access.decompress; DerivedArtifact + derived_written custody + DECOMP-NNN id; allowlist unchanged (10); CI-safe tests green.
